newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA WINS WOMEN'S SINGLES AT SKATE CANADA.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-SLUTSKAYA WINS WOMEN'S SINGLES AT SKATE CANADA.

text.p: Russia's Irina Slutskaya performed a flawless free-skating routine Saturday to clinch the women's singles title and a $30,000 prize at Skate Canada.

The 17-year-old Russian, who won the 1995 world junior title and was seventh at the '95 senior worlds, was hardly pressed as world number two Lu Chen of China withdrew after aggravating a foot injury in practice on Wednesday.
"I wish Lu had skated so we could have competed and fought for places," world number three Slutskaya said through an interpreter.
Second place, and a check for $18,000, went to 14-year-old American Tara Lipinski, with Switzerland's Lucinda Ruh, 17, finishing a surprising third to collect $10,000.
Lipinski, who stands 4-feet-8 (1.42 m) and weighs just 69 pounds (31 kg), was fourth at the '95 junior worlds and 15th at her first senior worlds last March in Edmonton.
"I skated good and I can build on this," she said. "I'm training really hard and my new coach and I are working really well together."
Ruh, who has lived most of her life in Japan where he father works as a chemical company executive, was 19th at the '96 worlds so standing on the podium was a career-boosting result.
